newsitem.title: GERMANY: Logistics expert sees Internet cargo bookings soon.
newsitem.headline: Logistics expert sees Internet cargo bookings soon.

text.p: Electronic cargo bookings through Internet transport services are likely in the near future, logistics expert Prof Heinz Isermann forecast to freight managers.

Isermann, professor of logistics and transport at Frankfurt University, said Internet information, communications and transactions services for the logistics industry were growing fast and already covered all sectors.

Air transport-related information was already so diverse with many airline and airport home pages that it was difficult to gain an overview, he said in a presentation to the German Logistics Congress in Berlin, which ended on Friday.
Isermann forecast: "American and some European airlines already offer their clients on-line bookings, so in future on-line bookings in the freight sector will probably also be possible.
"We are convinced that the Internet medium is an appropriate platform for freight markets but their functions must be matched to the individual needs of the different potential users," he added.
Integrators, parcels services and Lufthansa Cargo already offered tracking and tracing functions through Internet links to their own reservations systems, Isermann noted.
Internet offered the chance to link diverse corporate and other systems and develop electronic data exchange through the Edifact standard, he said.
